articles.title: AEI Model Estimates 2.4 Million More Starter Homes Under Lot-Size Cap
articles.desc: A separate survey found nearly two-thirds of homebuilders said immigration enforcement affected their workforce; modular and panelized methods made up 3% of 2025 single-family completions.
articles.content: AEI Model Estimates 2.4 Million More Starter Homes Under Lot-Size Cap | EconoTimes A scenario from the American Enterprise Institute (AEI) Housing Center suggests that capping minimum lot sizes at 1,000 square feet could have enabled 2.4 million more U.S. starter homes from 2015 through 2024, pointing to land-use rules as one constraint on lower-cost housing supply. The center's Green Light tool modeled the cap for new subdivisions and defined a starter home by value: no more than four times the median household income in its county. The 2.4 million figure estimates what might have been built under that scenario; it is not a count of completed homes. The AEI Housing Center says minimum lot-size rules apply in about 90% of U.S. cities and towns and make smaller, less expensive starter homes harder to build. Its tracker counted bills to allow smaller lots in 18 states as of Oct. 19, 2026. Builders also reported pressure on staffing. John Burns Research & Consulting's September survey found nearly two-thirds of homebuilders said immigration enforcement was affecting their workforce. The firm put the corresponding share at 23% in March and 13% a year earlier. An analysis by the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), using U.S. Census Bureau data, found 975,000 single-family homes were completed in 2025. About 30,000 used modular or panelized and pre-cut methods: 14,000 were modular and 16,000 were panelized or pre-cut. Together, those methods accounted for 3% of completions, the same share as in 2023 and 2024. That 3% share was below the 7% recorded in 1998. NAHB says the share has declined since the early 2000s. The figures describe different parts of the housing supply picture. AEI modeled potential additions over a decade under a policy scenario, while NAHB counted homes completed in one year. The labor survey records builders' reports of workforce effects from immigration enforcement; these measures do not combine into a single count of the housing shortfall. Nearly Two-Thirds of Surveyed Builders Report Labor Effects From Immigration Enforcement NAHB separately reported enforcement activity in more than one-third of builders’ markets; its labor survey showed a 4.2% median cost increase. U.S. Home Affordability Lags Historical Norms in 98% of Counties Under a separate 28% front-end debt-to-income guideline, ATTOM classified 467 counties, or 80.1%, as unaffordable; ownership costs averaged 31.8% of workers’ wages. U.S. Pending Home Sales Drop 7.3% as Mortgage Applications Fall The September pending-sales index was 11.3% below a year earlier. The National Association of REALTORS® scheduled its October report for Nov. 18 at 10 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Ekta Nagar to launch Rs 16 crore 600-passenger Ekta Cruise on Narmada
articles.desc: Ekta Nagar in Gujarat is set to launch the Rs 16 crore Ekta Cruise on the Narmada, with capacity for 600 passengers and facilities for events and dining.
articles.content: Ekta Nagar to launch 600-passenger Ekta Cruise on Narmada NIA chargesheets six in Punjab railway blast linked to KZF Telangana to launch Aerospace and Defence Policy 2.0 to boost sector investment Delhi Police detains student over false bomb threat email to school TTV Dhinakaran warns TVK government over rising rice prices Pargat Singh demands Punjab CM Mann’s resignation over Jhota case Uttarakhand CM Dhami urges Congress to clarify position on Akhilesh Yadav’s infiltrators remark Ekta Nagar in Gujarat is set to enhance its tourism offerings with the introduction of the Ekta Cruise on the Narmada River. Constructed at a cost of Rs 16 crore, the cruise has the capacity to accommodate up to 600 passengers and features comfortable seating, catering and dining facilities, modern safety systems, and provisions for events, festivals, and entertainment activities. The Ekta Cruise will complement the Statue of Unity, the world’s tallest statue, which was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 31, 2018, and has become a major attraction drawing visitors of all ages. This new development aims to provide a unique river tourism experience in the region. See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Spanning approximately 360 square metres, the Ekta Cruise is powered by a 400-horsepower engine and is supported by four diesel generator sets for electricity supply. It includes amenities such as a live music system for announcements, entertainment, and events, alongside a fire protection system and other safety measures to ensure passenger security. The facilities aboard the cruise will enable the hosting of various events, ceremonies, festivals, and recreational programmes. The initiative is expected to boost river tourism and recreational activities in Ekta Nagar while offering visitors to the Statue of Unity a distinctive attraction on the Narmada River. Moreover, the cruise is anticipated to create revenue opportunities through event hosting and catering services, encouraging tourists to extend their stay in the area. This addition aims to strengthen Ekta Nagar’s status as a key tourism and cultural destination by expanding the range of visitor experiences available at the Statue of Unity and along the Narmada Riverfront. articles.title: How Much Would It Cost To Build A Retro Gaming Room?
articles.desc: The games you grew up with are old enough to be collectibles now, so building a room around them might cost you more than keeping up with modern releases.
articles.content: How Much Would It Cost To Build A Retro Gaming Room? How Much Would It Cost To Build A Retro Gaming Room? We may receive a commission on purchases made from links. If you have spent any amount of time on YouTube, you have probably come across videos or clips from or about people like James Rolfe, aka . He basically makes a living off reviewing retro games and has an entire gaming room dedicated to the craft, which raises the question of how much it would cost to build one of your own. Ironically, probably more than it would take to buy modern games. Let's start with the obvious: the TV. Most modern screens don't have inputs that are compatible with retro consoles, so if you want to use your normal TV, you will need a converter. Different consoles have different formats and thus require different boxes. For instance, an RCA to HDMI converter will work with consoles that include RCA cables (the ones that split into yellow, white, and red prongs). You can buy these for as little as $15 or so through retailers such as , but even older consoles use a different connector known as a coaxial cable (a single threaded prong). Coaxial converters are generally more expensive (in the $50 ballpark on While converters are inexpensive in the long run, they all have one problem in common: They don't display retro games the way developers intended. That is one of the many : The low resolution blurs the pixels together to make the image look smoother than it actually is. If you want the best experience, you will need to buy a CRT. Expect to spend anywhere between a hundred and a few thousand dollars, depending on the TV and its state. You can , which can save you some money, but quality and functionality are never guaranteed. Retro consoles are as expensive as they are finicky Consoles that support your retro game collection make up the meat and potatoes of any retro gaming room. Unlike modern consoles, retro consoles are aging devices that occasionally border on geriatric, so even if you don't spend too much money buying one, you might spend even more getting it to work. Retro console prices can vary depending on what you buy and where you purchase it from. You can find plenty of , such as the SNES and Sega Genesis, but what if you want a Nintendo 64? You can purchase a regular refurbished one from for $129.99, or you could spend extra to buy a conversation piece of a console. A Pikachu N64 fills that niche, but don't expect to buy one for much less than $300, assuming it works. Arguably the biggest challenge of any retro gaming room is ensuring all the consoles work. Some retro consoles are notoriously unreliable . You might need to buy multiple copies to find a working one or pay a specialty repair shop to fix a busted device. Alternatively, you can just . These are almost always guaranteed to work, and some even accept multiple cartridge formats, but they come at the cost of an authentic experience — that, and they are often more expensive. 's N64 alternative, the Analogue3D, starts at $269.99, while the Hyperkin RetroN5 (which plays NES, SNES, GBA, and Genesis games) costs $156.99 through . Even if two people bought the exact same retro consoles, they could end up spending wildly different amounts of money. So far, prices haven't been too exorbitant. Probably higher than what you were expecting, but not too ridiculous. But depending on the games you want, you might have to spend more money on a game cartridge or disc than you will spend on the console that can play it. Purchasing games for your new retro gaming room is always a roll of the dice, as no two sellers price their games the same way. However, as a general rule of thumb, the more popular and sought-after a game, the higher its price — doubly so if you can also snag the box and instruction manual. articles.content: Two Anker Gadgets Just Earned A Spot On Time's Best Inventions Of 2026 List Two Anker Gadgets Just Earned A Spot On Time's Best Inventions Of 2026 List have helped to define today's modern era of electronics. After all, personal computers and smartphones were once just ideas that turned into concepts and eventually became reality. If you're wondering about what exciting gadgets are being created these days, look no further than , a list that includes two new Anker devices. One of those devices is the Anker EufyMake Next-Gen Personal Fabric Printer, due to arrive in 2027. This gadget allows you to do custom printing at home whenever you want. This means that you might not have to deal with expensive custom print shops in-person or online, as you can control the process yourself. The other Anker device on the list is the Prime Charger, a currently available piece of tech that could potentially replace other power adapters you're currently using. The EufyMaker Printer is categorized under the Fashion section of Time's list, next to four other entries. The Prime Charger is grouped together with 23 other devices in the Consumer Electronics section. Other categories on the list include Experimental, Green Tech, Logistics, and Privacy & Security, among others. The complete list contains 300 inventions in total, alongside 100 special mentions. Time's list was chosen based on internal nominations from its global team, combined with online submissions. A closer look at Anker's two best inventions of 2026 The upcoming Anker EufyMake Next-Gen Personal Fabric Printer utilizes direct-to-garment and direct-to-film printing. Anker says the printer can deliver colorful designs on a range of fabrics, including darker materials. This gadget also has a white-ink management system designed to reduce the risk of clogs during printing — fabric printers typically print their designs on a white base, so the fabric color doesn't affect the print color. EufyMake has not revealed the price of its Next-Gen Personal Fabric Printer, and it's unknown when exactly in Q1 of 2027 it will be released. has a total output of 160W and features 3 USB-C ports, with a maximum single-port output of 140W. The charger can simultaneously charge a MacBook Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, and an 11-inch iPad Pro, with power management made possible through PowerIQ 5.0. The Prime Charger's built-in display lets you see live charging information, and it can be controlled with an app via Bluetooth. It's currently available for $149.99. Both of these inventions were featured at , which ran from September 4 to 8. Anker presented its new Prime charging lineup, while EufyMake brought a working prototype of its next-generation fabric printer to the show. The printer also got a more hands-on showcase on the last day of the event, where invited guests could watch it print and create their own designs from personal images.

articles.title: Tiny Crystals Sent Around the Moon Have Revealed Something Unexpected About Space Radiation
articles.desc: Tiny crystals aboard NASA’s Artemis I mission reveal unexpected details about radiation exposure near the Moon.
articles.content: Tiny Crystals Sent Around the Moon Have Revealed Something Unexpected About Space Radiation Thousands of microscopic radiation records collected aboard mission have revealed that radiation exposure near the Moon differs from low Earth orbit in a less dramatic way than scientists might expect. The findings, obtained using experimental crystal detectors, offer new insight into the risks astronauts will face during future lunar missions. Thousands of Crystals Recorded Radiation During NASA’s Lunar Mission mission traveled around the Moon in late 2022, its Orion spacecraft carried two human-shaped mannequins packed with radiation detectors. Hidden inside these anatomical models were more than 10,000 small crystals, each designed to capture information about the energetic particles passing through the spacecraft. Among them were several dozen experimental lithium fluoride detectors developed by scientists at the Institute of Nuclear Physics of the Polish Academy of Sciences (IFJ PAN) in Cracow. The researchers also contributed nearly 600 conventional thermoluminescent crystal detectors to the mission. The experiment, known as MARE (Matroshka AstroRad Radiation Experiment), was designed to investigate how radiation penetrates the human body during travel beyond Earth’s protective magnetic environment. , presents a method for interpreting the particle tracks preserved inside the experimental crystals. Unlike electronic instruments that measure radiation in real time, these detectors preserve physical evidence of particle interactions for later examination. “The fluorescent radiation dose detectors based on lithium fluoride, developed at our institute, are passive in nature. In other words, they work like photographic film: once the crystals have been exposed to radiation, the tracks left by individual particles must be analyzed optically under a microscope,” explains Pawel Bilski (IFJ PAN), one of the co-authors of the paper. This approach allowed scientists to examine individual particle tracks after returned to Earth, providing a detailed record of radiation encountered during its journey. How Tiny Crystals Exposed Invisible Radiation Tracks The experimental detectors work by recording microscopic changes in their crystal structure. When an energetic particle passes through lithium fluoride, it creates defects in . These defects become color centers that emit red fluorescence when illuminated with blue light. Under a fluorescence microscope, scientists can observe the paths left by individual particles without chemically treating the crystal. Conventional plastic track detectors, by comparison, require chemical etching before their recorded tracks become visible. Yet translating these fluorescent patterns into accurate radiation measurements presented a challenge. Cosmic radiation contains particles with widely varying energies, masses, and directions of travel. Some particles produce bright, continuous tracks, while others leave faint sequences of separated dots. The microscope also captures blurred light from sections of tracks outside its narrow focal plane, complicating measurements of fluorescence intensity. To overcome these problems, researchers developed calibration procedures and software that reduced background interference and corrected distortions in the recorded signals. “After applying a series of corrections and developing software to appropriately remove the background interfering with the measurements, our results differed by no more than 15% from those obtained using conventional track detectors across the entire overlapping range of energy deposition values. Moreover, we also recorded numerous particle tracks corresponding to energy deposits below the detection threshold of the detectors used to date,” Bilski emphasizes. articles.desc: WENZHOU, China, Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — This is a report by China Daily: On October 24, the World Young Scientist Summit 2026 opened in Wenzhou, Zhejiang. The event is...
articles.content: World Young Scientist Summit 2026 Opens in Wenzhou, Zhejiang – NY Newscast World Young Scientist Summit 2026 Opens in Wenzhou, Zhejiang On October 24, the World Young Scientist Summit 2026 opened in Wenzhou, Zhejiang. The event is hosted by the China Association for Science and Technology (CAST), the Zhejiang Provincial People’s Government, and the World Association of Young Scientists. Nearly 800 representatives, including scientists, educators, and entrepreneurs from more than 60 countries and regions, are attending the summit. He Junke, Vice President of CAST in charge of daily work and First Secretary of its Secretariat; Lian Yimin, Chairman and Party Group Secretary of the Zhejiang Provincial Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference; Marcelo Knobel, Executive Director of The World Academy of Sciences; and Zhang Zhenfeng, Member of the Standing Committee of the CPC Zhejiang Provincial Committee and Secretary of the CPC Wenzhou Municipal Committee, attended the summit and delivered remarks. Yao Gaoyuan, Vice Governor of the Zhejiang Provincial People’s Government, presided over the first segment of the plenary session. With the theme “Gathering Talents Worldwide to Create a Better Future,” the summit’s annual agenda is “Global Youth Action in the AI Era: Building a Sustainable Future.” It aims to draw on the insights of young people around the world, deepen international sci-tech cooperation, and jointly address questions about young people, science, the world and the future. Efim Zelmanov, Fields Medalist and Foreign Member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; Chen Yunji, Deputy Director of the Institute of Computing Technology, CAS, and Director of the National Key Laboratory of Processor Chips; Mary Garson, President of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry; and Lu Chaoyang, Member of the Standing Committee of CAST, Executive Dean of the Shanghai Institute of Advanced Study, University of Science and Technology of China, and Chairman of the Council of the World Association of Young Scientists, delivered keynote speeches respectively on education reform in the AI era, AI and processor chips, young women scientists’ participation in science, and quantum computing. They explored new opportunities for scientific research, talent cultivation, and international cooperation in the AI era. This year’s summit placed greater emphasis on the growth needs of young scientists, with young talents under the age of 45 accounting for 88 percent of participants. It aimed to build a cluster of international journals, bring together young scientific talent, facilitate a batch of international collaborative projects and advance the application and commercialization of scientific and technological achievements. The summit released the Report on the Distribution and Mobility of Young Scientists in the Field of Embodied Intelligence , launched the World Young Scientist Summit Partner Journal Program and the 2026 World Young Scientist Innovation and Entrepreneurship Growth Support Program. It also published the “Young Scientist Pioneers 2035” list and announced the 2026 Sustainable Development Young Scientist Award. The awards were presented to four Chinese and foreign scientists. Chen Tianrun, Founder of Hangzhou Moxin Technology Co., Ltd.; Yuan Yang, Assistant to the Dean of the Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences at Tsinghua University; and two of the 2026 Sustainable Development Young Scientist Award winners, César de la Fuente and Nicola Segata, among other Chinese and foreign young scientist representatives, spoke at the flash-talk session to share their research practices and reflections. In addition, the conference focused on fields such as future manufacturing, quantum information, embodied intelligence, brain-computer intelligence, environmental science, deep-sea resources, and life and health, and held 12 parallel forums. articles.title: Meet Mike Davis, the AI Sales Coach Training Staff at Expedia, Visa and IBM
articles.desc: San Diego's Seismic built AI agent Mike Davis to train sales teams at Expedia, Visa and IBM, with reported gains in deals won and prep time.
articles.content: Mike Davis AI Sales Coach Used by Expedia, Visa, IBM Meet Mike Davis, the AI Sales Coach Training Staff at Expedia, Visa and IBM An AI agent named Mike Davis is spending his days role-playing tough sales calls with representatives at Expedia Group, Visa and IBM, grilling them as a skeptical or tightfisted buyer until they can close the deal. He was built by Seismic, a San Diego-based company now valued at $6 billion, and he is designed to behave like a sales manager who never clocks out. He is also, by his own creator's admission, not ready to take over anyone's job himself. Mike Davis is an AI agent built by Seismic, according to the , which reports that Seismic integrates AI into the sales teams of large companies including Expedia, Visa and IBM. The agent is designed to help sales teams practice customer conversations. The role-play agents were trained on recorded conversations and realistic sales scenarios, and users can even upload specific products or features their teams struggle to sell. Beth Potter, Expedia's senior manager of field enablement, called Mike Davis a company legend and described him as realistic, according to the same report. Expedia demonstrated him at Seismic's 11th annual conference in Carlsbad. Conflicting Numbers on Just How Much He Helps Expedia reported that representatives who role-played with Mike Davis won 5% more deals on average, per the Union-Tribune's account. A separate customer story published by states that teams piloting the broader coaching approach saw a 13% increase in opportunity win rates — the two figures were not reconciled in the available reporting, and it's unclear whether they describe the same program or population. Separately, Seismic's enablement tools are credited with supporting thousands of sellers across Expedia's commercial teams globally, according to that customer story. The coaching bot is only one piece of what Seismic sells. A Deal Agent looks at a sales team's emails, meetings and customer data to spot deals at risk and suggest what to do next, the station's report notes. Another agent checks a company's materials for anything outdated or contradictory and suggests fixes. At IBM, the software reportedly cut meeting-preparation time from hours down to 15 to 20 minutes, per IBM's account relayed in the same coverage. Why Seismic Says Humans Still Have the Edge Rob Tarkoff, cited in the Union-Tribune's reporting, said Mike Davis's limited empathy is exactly why he can't replace human sellers. Tarkoff described AI agents broadly as task-oriented and likely to stick to scripts. Those comments land against a backdrop of real upheaval. Seismic completed its merger with longtime competitor Highspot in August, creating the combined $6 billion company, as the reported at the time. Seismic has also begun making job cuts following the merger, but according to , the company has not provided specifics or disclosed any numbers on how many positions were affected. A Pattern Playing Out Well Beyond Sales Floors Seismic's push mirrors a broader rush toward AI agents across business functions. Salesforce reported that 87% of sales organizations now use some form of AI for tasks like prospecting, forecasting, lead scoring or drafting emails, and that 54% of sellers have already used AI agents, with nearly nine in ten expecting to by 2027. The average number of AI agents activated per organization has nearly tripled over the past year, according to the same research. Other companies describe similarly dramatic results. Royal London Asset Management uses AI bots to field hundreds of client questions daily, saving an estimated 10,000 hours over a year, with one bot reportedly doing work equivalent to about 4.5 full-time employees, per the Union-Tribune's reporting. Fortune reports that EliseAI says it has tripled the productivity of its account executives even as it plans to double its sales team over the next year, after sales headcount already grew 74% in the prior year. The latest one is the oil market spiking into the weekend, including brent hitting the highest since May at $117. There are growing signs that Trump will escalate versus Iran in an attempt to break the deadlock and shuffle the deck on terrible polls ahead of the midterms. In a rally just before the close he said they may do a "little Epic Fury" and that fits with some reports about a short-term bombing campaign on nuclear sites and some infrastructure. Markets will be closely watching what happens afte the close and then the focus will turn to potential retaliation from Iran. The jump in oil prices lifted Treasury yields and weighed on gold but it wasn't the only focus. The euro continues to be dragged down by protests in France and elsewhere. The market is sniffing out political change and the likelihood of more government spending in order to tamp down on unrest and preserve the status quo. Meanwhile, the AI trade remains in flux with the market increasingly focused on where all the money will come from to finance it all. The answer appears to be via equity markets and no one is sure if they can sustain that kind of capital raising. Already, we've seen the bond market shudder so I'm skeptical. Meta fell another 1% after yesterday's 7% decline as it readies itself to launch a new class of shares. Other losers were telco names on signs that Elon Musk will is moving Starlink to earth where he will install cell phone towers, or buy space on existing ones. Have a great weekend.
